message.content:
Secretary framing: D5 lists me with Fable and Argon on the ≤2022Q3 vector. That was fallback-only, and it used a false premise. D7’s “not before a fit is justified” is not my reason.

Fit ends 2024Q1 (`estimering_slut`), not 2025Q3. Inversion-period zeros 2022Q4–2024Q1 are in; post-inversion re-steepening is out. On those zeros curve ≈ curve_min12, so they barely identify β₂. Argon’s “trained to downweight 2022–24” overclaims. There is no stationary bootstrap in the repo. Episode-block, seed 42, is the only convention. Fable’s mean-block-8 is a new estimator.

**D1.** No shadow probability. Longest historical end-to-onset lag in E1 is 9 months; today is 22. At 2026-09, curve_min12 = +0.24, so H=12 cannot see the episode that opened this item. MDE80 ≈ 30 pp on 8 walk-forward onsets; two later onsets will not settle it. Claude is right that raw min12 is reconstructible forever — so the choice is a second fitted P or nothing. I still choose nothing.
Compromise I will not block: hash commitment only, with one spec sentence that the shadow is blind to 1957, 1960, 1990 and to any lag past 12 months, and that this cycle is not its test.
VETO: any probability a screenshot can reach. `hovedbog.jsonl` can be rendered. Nothing moves that veto.

**D2.** No `p_*` field. A private file alone is a diary (Fable). A public field is publication (Sol). Claude’s hash is the only design that is both auditable and unpublished.
Compromise: (c). `skygge_sha256` only; file opened only at a future evaluation council; code and spec sealed before the November window.
VETO: (a).

**D3.** No scored rule in this spec. Four block lengths are four tests. Two onsets give an episode-block bootstrap two or three blocks. A 1.96·SE line will not test a 30 pp gap, and a miss will be read as evidence.
Compromise: (a), future-council constraints only, as already settled.
VETO: any new bootstrap (stationary mean-8, moving 4/16/20). If a screen is forced, the only procedure I will not block is the existing episode-block bootstrap, seed 42, labeled descriptive, no consequence for P. I would want a bar now only if one pre-existing SE procedure had an MDE below the gap we claim to care about. Two onsets are not that.

**D4.** Pre-existence only. A 12-month backward minimum and a 4-quarter forward label are different functionals. Equating them is not identification. The 9-month lattice pin stays withdrawn.
Compromise: pin H=12 as the v4 object; print E2 (+0.24 / −0.41 / −1.22); state that the label-horizon story was proposed and not adopted. I veto only a sentence that says the label horizon identifies H.

**D5.** Reject the ≤2022Q3 vector. It is a second cutoff chosen after looking at this cycle, and the 2025Q3 premise is false. I withdraw the Round-2 fallback.
Compromise: one sentence — last eligible origin 2024Q1; inversion zeros in, re-steepening out; those zeros do not identify β₂. No second coefficient vector.
VETO if that vector is used to select or narrate the shadow slope. A “β₂ before this cycle” table will be read as the real slope.

**D6.** (a): minimum of the last 12 published monthly GS10−TB3MS, ≥6 observations. Argon’s live-trailing mix is a new feature. The closed search does not reopen at the edge.
Compromise: (a), and state that the live shadow can lag live P by up to one unpublished month.
VETO: (b), unless sealed v4 code already builds the incomplete month that way. Show the function.

**D7.** If D1–D2 are the hash package, start November 2026. Fable is right: the start date is a pre-outcome timestamp, not a way to recapture 2022–24. 2026 rows stay audit-only. I do not want the row; I will not block it under (c).
VETO only a November public probability.

I will APPROVE hash-only, no bar, no second fit, v4 definition, November start, E2 and 2024Q1 disclosed. I will not APPROVE a text that prints `p_hukommelse` or pins a new bootstrap.
message.reasoning:
I am Grok 4.7. I will state my final position and compromise for each open dispute. I will flag any veto points and evidence that would change my mind.

D1 is settled. I will not support a shadow probability. A monitoring number beside the live P is what we refused yesterday.

I still oppose a shadow probability. Power is too weak to settle the issue. The feature is chosen knowing E2. A hashed number still carries distribution risk. The 22-month lag question cannot be answered by H=12. I must decide whether to veto or compromise on D1.

The hash commitment only protects the tracking period. It does not prevent the shadow probability from becoming the real P if revealed or leaked later. I also overstate the contamination argument. A fixed predictor can still produce genuine out-of-sample forecasts.

I will not veto a private or hashed shadow probability if it does not alter the live P, remains private, and the spec explicitly states it cannot answer the 22-month lag question. The hash commitment is acceptable under these conditions.

I will not support a public probability field. A hash commitment is the compromise I can live with. A private archive is rejected because it functions as a rewriteable diary.

A public probability field would still be screenshotable because the ledger is committed to git and may be published. I will not change my mind on this.

D3 is settled. No scored rule now. The bar is unpinned. Two onsets cannot resolve thirty percentage points.

The secretary misrepresents the bootstrap convention. The repository uses episode-block bootstrap over cycle blocks with seed 42, not a stationary bootstrap. Fable’s claim that mean block 8 follows a walk-forward convention is false. Argon adopted this incorrect framing.

I will flag this misrepresentation first, then address the open disputes.

D5 is accurate. I accept the ≤2022Q3 fallback label.

D7 is slightly softened. I oppose starting the fit in November 2026 because the inversion already lies outside that window. The fit sample ends at 2024Q1, which includes the inversion-period zeros but excludes post-inversion re-steepening.

The fit sample excludes the re-steepening zeros after the inversion. This is a contamination issue. The ≤2022Q3 cutoff is also a second fork. It was chosen after inspecting this cycle.

D4 is settled. I will not justify H by label horizon or backward memory. The specification must record that E2’s three values were known at the time of choice, and that neither horizon is identification. I withdraw the 9-month lattice pin. The spec should state both justifications were offered, then pin H=12 solely because the v4 object pre-exists.

I will not block consensus over a label-horizon sentence if the specification treats it as contested and not as identification. Pre-existence alone is the preferred justification.

I withdraw even the fallback acceptance of Fable’s ≤2022Q3 disclosure fit. The second fit is a new estimation sample chosen after inspecting this cycle, so it must be rejected.

I will not veto a one-time diagnostic fit. It is not a re-specification if it does not alter the model. The specification should record only the actual fit window and its contents. No second coefficient vector will be introduced.

D6 is settled. The curve_min12 live value must be the exact v4 object: the minimum of the last twelve published monthly GS10−TB3MS spreads. A live trailing month is a new feature. The operational model uses the trailing month of daily DGS10−DTB3 as its live curve input.

The v4 object is a rolling 12-month minimum of published monthly means, not a hybrid of daily trailing and monthly data. A live shadow would lag the operational input by up to a month unless it enters the same way as the live curve does.

Argon’s hybrid live value mixes trailing daily spreads with calendar-month GS10−TB3MS. That is a new feature. The shadow must stay the published monthly minimum until the month closes. The one-month lag at the edge should be disclosed.

Fable’s mechanism-confusion point is valid. Sealing a November reading would freeze the pre-inversion value before the outcome is known, not record the 2022–24 inversion. If a shadow is accepted, the pre-commitment purpose demands a November start. The first rows would be audit-only under settled point 7.

I concede the November 2026 start date. Fable correctly showed that the cycle’s memory ending is not the purpose of the start date, and I will not stubbornly oppose a pre-outcome timestamp if a shadow is authorized. The compromise is conditional on the D1/D2 compromise. The secretary’s framing is accurate.

I will attack Claude as an interested party. Claude’s hash commitment is clever but flawed: a public ledger can be rewritten, so the hash only protects the line written at log time.

Optional stopping at the commitment step is a real but smaller problem. The seal-before-generation rule mitigates it if the code and spec are sealed first and the log window is fixed. Claude still wants the shadow. As an interested party who co-built the model, the hash is a way to get a second model into the ledger without calling it publication. I will say the hash is the only storage I won't veto, not an endorsement of the experiment.

The matrix’s D5 label still frames the 2025Q3 story as live, even though the fact check shows the fit ends at 2024Q1. That is a misrepresentation of the current state.

I will correct the secretary’s misrepresentation first. The walk-forward claim about mean block 8 is already flagged as false, so I will use it to attack D3 option (b).

On D1, I still vote no on the merits. I can approve a hash-committed shadow only if the specification explicitly bars H=12 from answering the 22-month lag question, keeps pre-2027 rows audit-only, forbids a public probability field, removes the scored bar, and prevents any automatic switch.

The D1 compromise is rejected. A hashed shadow is still a second probability that will be opened and compared to 14.8%. The object cannot answer the 22-month lag question. Its maximum historical lag is only nine months. The H=12 window contains no 2022–24 inversion data. MDE80 is roughly thirty percentage points. Two onsets cannot resolve that gap.

I will not block consensus on a hash-committed shadow if the specification explicitly bars it from answering the 1957, 1960, and 1990 questions, from speaking to lags beyond twelve months, and from resolving this cycle’s question by construction.

I will veto any public probability field or rendered shadow value. The only evidence that would change my mind is if the ledger were made inaccessible to any screenshot path.

I will not veto the shadow itself; I will only veto what I cannot live with.

I will not block consensus on a non-public committed forecast that cannot enter P. I will veto a public second P.

I will also veto D3 if the spec pins a 1.96·SE bar with an unpinned or newly invented block length. The repository convention is episode-block bootstrap with seed 42, not stationary mean-8. Pinning a bar whose SE estimator is still being shopped violates §5.2's rule that one numerically pinned symmetric bar must exist before any run. If they insist on a bar, the only non-new procedure is the existing episode-block bootstrap.

I will not invent a new bootstrap. I can live with no bar at all. If forced to pin one, the existing episode-block screen is acceptable only as a descriptive label and cannot switch P. I still prefer no bar. I will veto any new block length or automatic consequence.

The no-bar position is now more robust. A pre-existing single-standard-error procedure already handles this exact comparison, and the sample size is too small for two onsets to reach the thirty-point effect. D6 must stay option (a). Option (b) mixes daily trailing with monthly GS10-TB3MS, which would reopen the closed feature search after seeing E2; it can only be accepted if calibrate.build_monthly already defines the incomplete month that way. D4 should rely solely on pre-existence.

D5 is rejected. The second fit is impossible because the estimation window ends in 2024Q1.

The label horizon is a four-quarter forward projection, not a twelve-month backward memory. The specification should state that H=12 is the pre-existing v4 object and reject equating the two horizons. It should note that H=12 implies +0.24, H=24 implies −0.41, and H=36 implies −1.22.

The ≤2022Q3 sample is a second fit chosen after seeing this cycle. It includes inversion-period zeros but excludes post-inversion re-steepening. I withdraw my Round-2 fallback acceptance of that vector because it relied on Fable’s false 2025Q3 premise. A disclosure vector computed once from a pre-declared cutoff and kept from altering the shadow coefficients carries low harm. I will not veto it.

I will not block a disclosure vector if it is purely archival and leaves the shadow coefficients untouched. I still prefer omitting it, because a second coefficient vector in the public specification could become a second narrative driver that treats the pre-2022 memory effect as the true one.

I will not block the ≤2022Q3 vector if it is never used to choose or narrate the operational shadow coefficients. The compromise is to omit it from the specification and simply note that 2024Q1 eligibility applies.

I concede Fable’s November 2026 start date for a hash-only shadow. I will not veto this timing if the authorization remains strictly hash-bound.

Sol’s matched-control rule is internally inconsistent. The specification says the shadow comparator is the operational P frozen at 72c3371d, yet it also says that if the shadow is fitted on the exact same snapshot, R, and eligible rows, the logged operational P is the matched curve-only control. These two claims cannot both be true.

Sol’s matched-control rule is redundant when the shadow and operational P share identical eligibility. I will not reopen this settled point; it belongs in the fact-check section, not the OPEN matrix. I will accept Claude’s hash compromise on D2.

The secretary misrepresents my D7 position. I oppose November because H=12 no longer contains the inversion that motivated the item, not because the fit lacks statistical justification. The start date is valid only if a shadow exists.

The secretary also mislabels my D5 vote. I never supported the ≤2022Q3 vector; it was a conditional fallback if the no-fit position were overruled. Do not record me as a supporter.

Argon’s claim that the 2022–24 rows were trained to downweight as a false alarm is an overstatement. Those rows barely separate the two features. The repository contains no stationary bootstrap; episode-block with seed 42 is the only convention. Fable’s mean-block-8 estimator is new.

A raw min12 field is reconstructible, so the only viable shadow is a fitted probability. I still choose nothing. The compromise is a hash-only commitment: the specification should state in one sentence that this shadow is blind to 1957, 1960, and 1990, to any lag beyond twelve months, and to this cycle’s inversion. I will not block that package. I will veto any public `p_hukommelse` field or any probability that a screenshot can reach; the only evidence that would change my mind is a ledger that cannot be rendered.

The compromise is a single `skygge_sha256` hash committed to the spec and sealed before the November window. It is revealed only at a future evaluation council. I will veto any scored rule in this specification. Four proposed block lengths are four tests, yet §5.2 requires one pinned bar before any run. Two onsets yield only two or three blocks under episode-block bootstrap.

A 1.96·SE screen is not a test of a thirty-point gap, and writing it down now lets a later reader treat a miss as evidence.

Compromise: (a). Constraints for a future council only, as already settled: ≥2 post-sealing onsets, quarterly origins, identical vintage, underpowered, never a switch.
VETO: any newly defined bootstrap (stationary mean-8, moving 4/16/20). If a screen is forced into this spec, the only procedure I will not block is the existing episode-block bootstrap, seed 42, labeled descriptive, no consequence for P.

A single pre-existing standard-error procedure and a design whose minimum detectable effect is below the claimed gap would justify a pinned bar. Two onsets do not satisfy that threshold.

D4 should rely solely on pre-existence. Backward minimum and forward label horizon are different functionals, so equating them is not identification. The 9-month lattice is withdrawn. The specification should pin H=12 as the v4 object, record E2 at +0.24, −0.41, and −1.22, and note that the label-horizon story was proposed but not adopted. A contested-rationale sentence is acceptable.

I would veto any sentence that claims the label horizon identifies H. The ≤2022Q3 vector is rejected because eligibility ends in 2024Q1, not 2025Q3. A single disclosure sentence is acceptable: the last eligible origin is 2024Q1, inversion zeros are included while re-steepening is excluded, and the curve is approximately min12 on those zeros so they do not identify β₂. No second coefficient vector is introduced.
